q: The source coding theorem (Shannon's first theorem) states that a source with entropy H can be compressed to an average code length arbitrarily close to:
opts: H bits per symbol (and no less)
log|A| bits per symbol where |A| is the alphabet size
exp: Shannon's source coding theorem: the minimum average description length per symbol approaches H(X) bits. Any lossless code requires average length ≥ H(X), and Huffman codes achieve lengths < H(X) + 1.
